name: Australia
summary: Community pack for Australia: band names from the ACMA spectrum plan, 433 MHz tyre sensors and fobs, km/h, plate-reader makers used in Australia. In testing: expect mislabels and report them.

rules.note: Genetec Inc. (Montreal) MA-L blocks. In Australia Genetec AutoVu Sharp plate readers run parking enforcement and car-park access. The same registrant ships Security Center servers, access control and ordinary CCTV, so a hit means Genetec hardware, not necessarily a plate reader. Weight sits under enterprise-camera-oui (80) so the card keeps CAMERA and gains this note. 00:0A:B1 (GENETEC Corporation, Japan) is a different company and excluded
Adaptive Recognition Hungary (Carmen ANPR engine, Vidar/MicroCam ANPR cameras). The same registrant makes passport/document readers, so POSSIBLE
MTData Developments Pty (Melbourne): vehicle telematics and driver terminals in Australian trucking, bus and council fleets. Listed, never alerted
Navman New Zealand MA-L block: Teletrac Navman fleet tracking units, common in Australian commercial fleets. Older Navman consumer sat-navs share the registrant
MiX Telematics: fleet tracking and driver cameras used by Australian mining, oil and gas, and bus fleets
Cohda Wireless Pty (Adelaide): V2X / C-ITS roadside units and vehicle radios used in Australian connected-vehicle trials. A hit may also be a test vehicle's on-board unit
Redarc Electronics (Adelaide): 12 V battery managers, brake controllers and caravan electrics with Bluetooth apps

notes: Speed-measuring devices are not detected: using a radar or speed-camera detector is an offence in every Australian state and territory (WA banned them from October 2020), and some definitions cover any device that detects speed-measuring equipment. Rules for speed-enforcement makers are switched off in this pack.

Plate readers: Elsag, Neology (formerly PIPS), Tattile, Kapsch and Motorola rules apply everywhere; this pack adds Genetec AutoVu (parking) and Adaptive Recognition, plus Australian fleet makers (MTData, Teletrac Navman, MiX) as non-alerting fleet hardware. Some systems in use in Australia publish no radio identifiers, so they are not detected.
Band names come from the ACMA spectrum plan. A frequency the pack does not name shows as a plain carrier rather than a US label.
Remote ID is not mandated in Australia, so fewer drones announce themselves; DJI's own broadcast still works.
